# HYB26-skill

Build, improve, debug, check, and safely copy GitHub Universe 2026 badge apps.
The Mac and Windows packages provide the same badge features and Python tools.
Install only the package for your computer; both use the name `hyb26-skill`.

**Custom app menu icons are not supported yet on the current event firmware.**
The starter's `icon.png` is a preview image only. Changing it will not change
the badge menu. Images drawn inside your app are a separate, supported feature.

## Install and check

<!-- platform:start -->
On Mac, install Python 3.10 or newer. Open Terminal in this complete skill
folder and run:

```bash
sh ./install-skill.sh
copilot skill list
```

The installer copies the package to `$HOME/.copilot/skills/hyb26-skill`.
Run it again from a newer copy to update. It preserves unrelated existing
files. See `INSTALL.txt` for repository-local installation and checks.
<!-- platform:end -->

If Copilot CLI is already open, use `/skills reload` or restart the session.
For another Copilot client, verify its documented skill locations and use a
test prompt; this installer does not change that client's settings or models.

## Use it for

- Turning an idea into an app under `badge/apps/<name>`.
- Choosing screens, controls, assets, state, and bounded memory use.
- Reusing verified motion, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, IR, lights, and battery patterns.
- Creating an app, checking its files, and listing readable badge source.
- Previewing and copying one app, with a backup before an intended replacement.
- Identifying which features still need tests on a real badge.

Open your badge project folder, then ask Copilot to use `hyb26-skill`.
A plain folder is enough; a repository is optional. Host-specific commands
for all four app tools are in [SKILL.md](SKILL.md).

Deployment previews by default. `--write` copies only the selected app;
`--replace` permits replacement with a backup. Credentials, hidden files,
and generated bytecode are excluded. Do not copy apps to RP2350.

## Evidence and limits

Shared references include the current event badge's menu behavior and pinned
first-party repository sources. See [references/sources.md](references/sources.md)
for the source order and known disagreements. Older repository examples can
lag current firmware; do not treat them as the final authority for menu icons.

Static checks and desktop previews do not prove physical badge compatibility.
Use the hardware checklists, and report tests that have not been done.

## Maintenance

Run the package's Python tests and the workspace comparison check after an
update. `TEST.md` contains prompts for checking the assistant's behavior.
Both packages must keep matching Python tools, tests, references, and feature
instructions; only marked host-command sections and installation files differ.
